title: Chord Study (piano)
description: Chords of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 notes in both hands: close and open positions, seconds (displaced noteheads), accidentals inside chords, beamed eighth- and 16th-note chords, dotted and whole-note chords, chords with ledger lines.

expected.notes: ONE part (Piano) on a grand staff (2 staves), 10 bars of 4/4; every simultaneity is a chord on one stem (must stay a chord, not separate voices or parts). Chord sizes per counts_detail; 6-note chords in bars 2 and 9 (RH) and bar 9 (LH).

count_rules._scope: Counts are read from truth.musicxml. "Main notes" = <note> elements with <pitch> that are neither <grace/> nor <cue/>; note-family tags count main notes only, grace and cue notes are counted by grace / grace-slash / cue-note. Cross-checked against the LilyPond engraving (grob dump).
count_rules.note-<value>: main noteheads (<note> elements, chord tones included) with that <type>; two-note-tremolo notes count with their printed type
count_rules.dot: main noteheads with exactly one <dot/> (every head of a dotted chord carries its own dot)
count_rules.chord: main chord events: a note without <chord/> followed by >= 1 <chord/> notes (sizes in counts_detail)
count_rules.beam: beam groups among main notes (= <beam number="1">begin</beam>); grace beam groups in counts_detail
count_rules.flag: main stems (chord = one stem) of value eighth or shorter without <beam> and not in a two-note tremolo
count_rules.stem-up / stem-down: main stems (chord = one stem) with <stem>up</stem> / <stem>down</stem>; whole notes and breves have no stem
count_rules.ledger-above / ledger-below: main noteheads that need >= 1 ledger line above / below the 5-line staff (staff position from pitch and the clef in force); per-depth numbers in counts_detail (ledger-above-1 .. -5 = heads needing exactly n lines)
count_rules.tremolo: tremolo marks: single-note tremolos (per stem) + two-note tremolos (per pair, type="start")
count_rules.rest-whole-bar: <rest measure="yes"/> (each bar of a multi-bar rest counts)
count_rules.acc-*: printed <accidental> elements on any note (main, grace or cue)
count_rules.clef-*: <clef> elements (one per staff at the start)
count_rules.clef-change: <clef> elements after the first attributes of the part
count_rules.time-*: <time> elements (C / cut symbol counted as time-common / time-cut only)
count_rules.slur: <slur type="start"> (includes the slur LilyPond draws for \acciaccatura/\appoggiatura)
count_rules.multi-page: 1 when the engraving has more than one page
count_rules.text-expression: <words> directions that are not tempo marks (bold measure-start words)

notes: Every stemmed note carries <stem>: the engraving is forced to exactly that direction (standard middle-line rule, the extreme note of a chord / beam group / two-note tremolo decides, middle line goes down; graces up; explicit \stemUp/\stemDown passages kept). Whole notes and breves carry no <stem>.

<beam> elements reproduce the engraved beams level by level (manual beaming): level 1 joins the whole group, a secondary level joins neighbours that both carry it; a rest inside a beam carries no <beam> element but a 16th rest between 16ths keeps the secondary beam continuous (as LilyPond draws it), so the note after it continues the level; beamlets are forward/backward hooks.
chord counts chord events (one stem); chord tones are counted as noteheads in note-<value>.
license_detail: CC0-1.0: composition, engraving, truth and scans created for this corpus

validation.method: LilyPond 2.24 run with an instrumented dump (nsynth/dump.ly): every note/rest event (onset, pitch, notated type, dots, tuplet scale, grace offset), tie, beam start/stop, slur, tremolo, time signature, bar number/measure position; every Stem of the final layout (direction, duration log, beamed, beams/beamlets left and right, stem-tremolo strokes, heads) and every NoteHead (staff position -> ledger lines, head type, font size for grace/cue); every printed accidental. All compared with the model the truth is written from; plus LilyPond MIDI attacks, a music21 re-parse of truth.musicxml and xmllint against MusicXML 4.0 XSD. The symbol counts in this file are read back from truth.musicxml (nsynth/counts.py) and must equal the counts measured on the engraving.
